reviews.title: Foundation architecture · asynchronous planning review
reviews.body:
Producer brief: Rust engine_core/game_core/game_web with wgpu + hecs, a TypeScript shell for audio, saves and PWA; a local-private production interface; three enemy families and one boss generation each for the initial slice.

Production reviewer response: Keep the production dashboard independent of the game. Task Active is a work state, not proof an agent is currently running. Use revision checks, recorded acceptance evidence and real participant contributions. Scope the game's service worker away from the dashboard and API.

Outcome: producer assigned the dashboard/API implementation and parallel engine, gameplay and web-shell work. No implementation checks or playable builds were reported in this planning discussion.
reviews.author: Production specialist
reviews.source: Actual producer–production specialist messages and review response in the current Codex session, 11 October 2026 Brisbane time.

reviews.title: Save persistence and dock-safe PWA update review
reviews.body: Production specialist reproduced five save failure groups before making corrections: profile normalization without revision changes, exposed mutable recovery snapshots, import ordering and stale-session overwrites, unavailable storage reporting import success, and competing open sessions replacing newer progression. storage.ts now validates nonzero seeds and signature ranks, clones snapshots, serializes imports with saves, rejects unpersistable imports, freezes the replaced session until reload, and compares persisted state before committing a normal save. Producer changed PWA generation to hash sorted paths and contents, wait for ACTIVATE_AT_DOCK, and activate after a saved dock interaction. QA ran 8 fake-indexeddb SaveStore tests and 4 tests against the actual generated service worker in an isolated VM: all 12 passed. The tests cover real IndexedDB API transactions through fake-indexeddb and simulated worker events; browser install, real offline reload, and physical phone performance remain for integrated acceptance. Root is handling browser checks and final task acceptance.
reviews.author: Production specialist / QA
reviews.source: Actual asynchronous Producer and Production specialist exchange in the current Codex session; Node test output work/save-pwa-tests.log

reviews.title: Schema 2 migration and claimed-reward semantics
reviews.body: Producer requested schema 2 discoveries, quests and relics with bounded grid identifiers, plus reduced motion/cosmetic settings. Production specialist implemented canonical v1-to-v2 normalization, preserving revision, seed, currency, ranks and existing progression, migrating current/previous snapshots and legacy imports, validating bounded unique lists and quest fields, and comparing normalized state for cross-session save conflicts. Thirteen fake-indexeddb/settings tests passed; evidence is work/storage-v2-tests.log. Gameplay specialist confirmed the runtime contract and clarified that completed means reward claimed, while progress at target means ready. Runtime separately checks IDs against seeded sites and may increment revision when courier cargo is delivered at Haven on reload. Claiming grants three category currency and one unique relic; repeating a claim errors. Storage format migration itself changes no reward or revision. Integrated browser acceptance remains with Producer. This record summarizes an actual asynchronous exchange, not a scheduled meeting.
reviews.author: Production specialist
reviews.source: Actual Producer assignment, Production specialist implementation/test evidence, and Gameplay specialist schema/reward clarification in the current asynchronous Codex exchange

reviews.title: Generated atlas silhouettes and interface cell conversion
reviews.body: Producer supplied the real transparent sprite and UI atlas artifacts, specified crop boundaries and bounded frame sizes, and required preservation of all logo components. Production specialist converted the sheets into individual indexed cell data with hard alpha, shared 64-entry palettes and nearest sampling. UI assets contain 15,528 logo cells, 3,475 panel cells, 1,417 button cells and 804 seal cells. Data and visual checks passed for exact dimensions, bounded row-major indices, sampled silhouettes, alpha128, disconnected component preservation, centered aspect fit and byte-identical atlas/preview/provenance reruns; work/ui-atlas-tests.log contains evidence. Local Tiny5 and supplied OFL file hashes are retained in UI provenance. Gameplay specialist reported prior sprite integration with exact occupancy, including 1,067-cell asteroid variants, and requested a read-only orientation/silhouette review. Production specialist verified north-facing art aligns through heading plus FRAC_PI_2, intentional dock/crater gaps and narrow linked Coil modules; no crucial art blocker was found. The UI JSON contract was handed to Engine specialist, while UI state/layout integration and browser checks remain active under Producer. This is a record of actual asynchronous contributions.

decisions.body: Producer relayed the user's selected direction: solo local progression, PWA distribution, neo-retro cosmic visuals, target 60 FPS on midrange phones, and a playable slice developed alongside the production interface. The first slice includes three enemy families, one boss generation each, six upgrades and three signature abilities; all five boss generations per family remain later work.

decisions.title: UI is drawn by the pixel engine; world discoveries remain deterministic
decisions.body: Generated UI is thresholded, nearest-resampled and palette indexed into real occupied cells. Semantic DOM retains accessibility and pointer capture while Rust renders UI groups after world layers. Settings include reduced motion and reduced cosmetic density. Seeded jittered region grids add sanctuary events, courier deliveries and family bounties; schema 2 migrates old progression. Invite-based co-op is a future milestone.

decisions.title: Accepted future dock ownership and separate circular battle royale
decisions.body: The Producer relayed the user-approved future direction: owned docks gain protection-radius upgrades and arenas; a separate multiplayer battle royale uses a compact seeded circular universe with equally spaced zones, arena sieges and a last-player-standing outcome. Crossing its outer edge places the ship at the antipodal edge, preserves heading and speed, and rebases the camera. This records direction only. Costs, radius bounds, zone contents, player counts, siege/elimination rules, match length and networking remain future design/implementation. Invite co-op and authoritative sessions remain backlog prerequisites. Current playable delivery remains a solo PWA slice. See docs/ROADMAP.md and the linked backlog tasks.
